body:
This appears to be an issue with the implementation of `takeUntilDestroyed`. If you replace it with a manual `destroyed$` subject that's `next`ed in an `ngOnDestroy` everything works fine.

I think what's happening is that the `takeUntilDestroyed` is unregistering its onDestroy callbacks during the destroy process, but doing so mutates the ON_DESTROY_HOOKS array while the framework is iterating over it, which causes some entries to be skipped.

Specifically, the ON_DESTROY_HOOKS array is used here: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/cc286be7af31c7f999d6c469d3fd8f9becb28ce7/packages/core/src/render3/node_manipulation.ts#L468-L476

and `takeUntilDestroyed`'s onDestroy callback calls this function: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/cc286be7af31c7f999d6c469d3fd8f9becb28ce7/packages/core/src/render3/util/view_utils.ts#L230-L237

which mutates the internal ON_DESTROY_HOOKS array (see the `splice` call on line 235).

The more `takeUntilDestroyed`s you have, the more onDestroy callbacks you're going to skip. I believe this explains all the behavior shown in your reproduction. The "unregister" behavior of the `takeUntilDestroyed` function is desirable because it unregisters onDestroy callbacks when the RxJS subscription is unsubscribed, so I think the fix for this is to simply shallow copy the ON_DESTROY_HOOKS array before iterating over it. I'd be happy to create a PR for this if the team is open to it.

Thnx for reporting @wartab - this is definitively an unfortunate bug - thnx for reporting.

Here is a smaller reproduce scenario for the case (1) - and I presume that other cases are similar: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-wffadt?file=src%2Fmain.ts

What is happening here is that we are modifying an internal array (one storing destroy callbacks) _while iterating over it_. 

I'm going to look into the fix.

@garrettld ha ha - it looks like we were doing the same investigation at the same time :-) Happy to see that our analysis is the same and points at the same root cause.

As for the PR - go for it! We just need to make sure that we've got proper tests for it (it should be possible to create one without `takeUntilDestroyed` and just `DestroyRef`, I think ?).

~~In terms of the fix: shallow clone would be an option, but doing for..of loop (using the iterator protocol) might do the trick as well.~~ (it does not...). Alternatively we could ignore unregistration if a view is already destroyed. Or assign the `lView[ON_DESTROY_HOOKS]` collection to an intermediate variable (before iterating) and do `lView[ON_DESTROY_HOOKS] = null;`.

Feel free to ping me if you need any help creating a PR.
Thank you for looking into this. I tried to investigate it myself, but it was too late for me to make sense of Angular internals I'm unfamiliar with.

issue.body:
Ensure that all onDestroy callbacks are called by allowing unregistering of onDestroy hooks while destroying.

Fixes #50221

- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.io application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:


## What is the current behavior?
<!-- Please describe the current behavior that you are modifying, or link to a relevant issue. -->
`onDestroy` callbacks that unregister themselves when called will cause the next `onDestroy` callback to be skipped.

Issue Number: #50221


## What is the new behavior?
All `onDestroy` callbacks that are present when the destroy process starts will be called, regardless of any unregistration that may occur while destroying.

Is this fixes the problem when using multiple `takeUntilDestroyed` in the same component only first occurrence to be unsubscribed?

```typescript
interval(1000).pipe(
  takeUntilDestroyed(this.destroyRef),
).subscribe(e => console.log(`tick 1: ${e}`));

interval(1000).pipe(
  takeUntilDestroyed(this.destroyRef),
).subscribe(e => console.log(`tick 2: ${e}`));

this.destroyRef.onDestroy(() => console.log("onDestroy"));
```

```
tick 1: 0
tick 2: 0
tick 1: 1
tick 2: 1
tick 1: 2
tick 2: 2
...
onDestroy
tick 2: 7
tick 2: 8
tick 2: 9
tick 2: 10
tick 2: 11
tick 2: 12
tick 2: 13
tick 2: 14
```
@dcby Yes, the scenario you described has the same root cause as this issue, and both should be fixed whenever the fix is released (I assume the next patch release, 16.0.2).
